Description: The project standard is Telerik UI for Blazor: one consistent look, behavior and accessibility story
Do: Use the matching Telerik component (Grid, Form, DropDownList, DatePicker, Window, Dialog ...) and its theme; native HTML only where no suitable Telerik component exists
Don't: Mixing a second component library or hand-built clones of Telerik components
Code Bad: <input type="date" class="my-custom-date" /> next to Telerik inputs

Description: It provides settings (icon type, RTL) to all Telerik components and renders their popups on top of the page; popup components throw without it
Do: Put TelerikRootComponent around @Body in the main layout
Don't: Telerik Window, Dialog or DropDown without a root component
Code Bad: @Body with a TelerikWindow somewhere inside and no root component

Guideline: Choose one built-in theme and customize through swatches or ThemeBuilder
Description: Telerik ships Default, Bootstrap, Fluent and Material themes with color swatches
Do: Load a single theme stylesheet and adjust it with a swatch or ThemeBuilder output
Don't: Overriding component internals with ad-hoc CSS or loading two themes
Code Good: One theme stylesheet reference in the host page head
Code Bad: Several theme stylesheets plus many !important overrides

Guideline: Use OnRead for large data and never combine it with Data
Description: OnRead lets the server filter, sort and page; Data plus OnRead on one component is not supported
Do: Handle OnRead and return only the requested page: args.Data and args.Total
Don't: Loading the whole table into memory and binding it with Data
Code Good: async Task OnRead(GridReadEventArgs args) { var r = query.ToDataSourceResult(args.Request); args.Data = r.Data; args.Total = r.Total; }

Guideline: Pass an IQueryable DTO projection to ToDataSourceResult
Description: ToDataSourceResult accepts IQueryable, so filtering, sorting and paging can translate to SQL; project to the needed columns first (less I/O, memory, network)
Do: Select into a narrow DTO on the IQueryable, then call ToDataSourceResult(args.Request); see sql-optimization.md
Don't: ToList() before the data request or selecting full entities for a grid
Code Good: var r = db.Orders.AsNoTracking().Select(o => new OrderRow(o.Id, o.Number, o.Total)).ToDataSourceResult(args.Request);

Guideline: Virtual scrolling needs ScrollMode, Height, RowHeight and PageSize, with equal row heights
Description: Row virtualization breaks when rows differ in height; Height must not show the whole PageSize at once
Do: Set ScrollMode=Virtual, a CSS Height, a decimal RowHeight (px) that fits the tallest cell, and a PageSize
Don't: Wrapping or variable-height cells in a virtual Grid

Description: The Form validates through DataAnnotationsValidator or any EditContext-compatible validator such as FluentValidation
Do: Nest FormValidation with the validator inside TelerikForm and handle OnValidSubmit
Don't: Hand-rolled validation state and manual error labels
Code Bad: <TelerikForm Model="@model"> with if-chains in the submit handler

Guideline: Use the Telerik validation components for messages
Description: TelerikValidationSummary, TelerikValidationMessage and TelerikValidationTooltip support templates and localization
Do: Place the Telerik validation component next to the field or at the top of the form
Don't: Custom red text spans that screen readers do not announce

Guideline: Rely on the built-in WCAG 2.2 AA keyboard and ARIA behavior
Description: Telerik components target WCAG 2.2; replacing them with clickable divs loses focus handling, roles and keyboard support
Do: Use the Telerik component or a native control, label every input, keep visible focus
Don't: div or span with @onclick standing in for a button or link

Guideline: Prefer SVG icons through the typed SvgIcon object
Description: SVG icons give better accessibility and multi-color support; font icons have a smaller HTML footprint
Do: Pass a value of the built-in SvgIcon object to the Icon parameter and add the Telerik.SvgIcons using
Don't: Magic strings for icon names or pasted inline SVG markup

Guideline: Use the DialogFactory predefined dialogs instead of browser alert and confirm
Description: Predefined alert, confirm and prompt dialogs match the theme and need no JS interop of your own
Do: Cascade DialogFactory and await its Alert, Confirm or Prompt methods
Code Good: if (await Dialogs.ConfirmAsync("Delete the record?")) { await Delete(); }

Guideline: Dialog for modal decisions, Window for movable or resizable content
Description: A Dialog is a modal Window that cannot be dragged or resized and has a built-in action-button footer
Do: Pick Dialog for confirmations and short forms, Window for tool panels
Don't: A Window used as a plain modal confirmation

Guideline: Localize built-in Telerik texts through ITelerikStringLocalizer or TelerikMessages resx
Description: Component texts resolve through ITelerikStringLocalizer; resx files named TelerikMessages.<locale>.resx are the standard way; register a custom localizer after AddTelerikBlazor
Do: Add the Hungarian resx (or a localizer) and re-check it on every Telerik upgrade
Don't: Leaving built-in English texts in a Hungarian app

Guideline: bUnit with Telerik: register services, loose JSInterop, add a root component
Description: Telerik components rely on JS interop and popups need TelerikRootComponent; some scenarios are not unit-testable and belong in browser e2e tests
Do: Services.AddTelerikBlazor(), JSInterop.Mode = JSRuntimeMode.Loose, render inside TelerikRootComponent when a popup is involved; cover the rest with Playwright
Don't: Asserting that Telerik itself sorts or pages
Code Bad: Rendering a TelerikWindow in bUnit without a root component

Guideline: Never commit the Telerik license key; use the TELERIK_LICENSE secret in CI
Description: A key is needed for build, for tests unless dotnet test uses --no-build, and for publish unless --no-build; telerik-license.txt must stay out of source control and plain-text workflows
Do: Store the key as a CI secret exposed as TELERIK_LICENSE (or a protected license file via TELERIK_LICENSE_PATH)
Don't: Committing telerik-license.txt or writing the key into a workflow file

Guideline: Authenticate the Telerik NuGet feed with a secret API key
Description: The feed is https://nuget.telerik.com/v3/index.json (no trailing slash), user name api-key, password is your API key; the key must never be checked in
Do: Reference an environment variable for the password in NuGet.Config or add the source in the pipeline from a secret
Don't: A plain-text API key in NuGet.Config or a trailing slash in the feed URL
